name: manual_591f16
claim: When another agent's uncommitted work is found sitting in a shared checkout, do not assume it is either live-in-progress OR safe-to-discard from presence alone -- verify liveness independently per artifact type. For code changes tied to a specific PR/CI problem: check the PR's actual current state (gh pr view --json state,statusCheckRollup) and whether the underlying CI job is already green without the change -- a fix left uncommitted can be stale because the real fix already landed a different way. For memory/lesson commits: verify correctness of content instead (does the claim hold up, is it properly anonymized) rather than staleness, since memory entries don't go stale the way code fixes do.

decisions.notes: 2026-07-22: found two artifacts from the same concurrent agent (ClinePass-DeepSeek-v4-flash) in the same session -- an uncommitted repo_hygiene.py/check_identity.sh edit from a 2026-07-19 PR190 handoff (turned out stale: PR190 already merged 3 days ago with Git hygiene passing, the runtime private_owner_email_ok() check already covered the case, discarding was correct) and a same-session memory-lesson commit (turned out legitimate: well-formed, correctly anonymized, reached the same conclusion independently). Treating both under one blanket rule (either 'always trust' or 'always discard') would have been wrong for one of the two.
